assessments.tested_scope: Haddouche & Sakhi 2026 Appendix C dynamic/off-policy theorem under bounded costs, current-batch conditional assumptions and its policy representation.
assessments.rationale: Primary proof gives an exact cumulative KL path term sum KL(Q_k||Q_{k-1}) with predictable previous-posterior reference and time-uniform average sequential-risk control. The theorem is direct; the proposed two-mode scheduler is not.
limits: Targets average sequential risk under changing contexts, not one final stationary policy.
Does not detect when to switch between stable and drift modes.
No autonomous-agent end-to-end validation.

assessments.tested_scope: Nonparametric e-detector false-alarm/delay guarantees plus separate dynamic off-policy theorem.
assessments.rationale: Both components have primary formal guarantees; e-detectors provide nonasymptotic false-alarm control and near-optimal delay in specified regimes, while the learner has a dynamic-risk theorem.
limits: No theorem or matched experiment validates the composed detector-to-memory-switch controller.
Monitored statistic may miss semantic drift.
Reset/recurring-regime semantics remain open.

assessments.tested_scope: Predeclared countable counterfactual test universe; fixed-candidate valid e-processes; weighted Ville/union correction for adaptive selection.
assessments.rationale: The derivation is mechanically checkable and directly repairs a concrete reused-validation memorization attack. Dwork-style description-length validity and e-process/FWER theory support the ingredients.
limits: Not a named published theorem in this exact form.
Requires complete encoding of all validation-dependent side channels.
Can be prohibitively conservative when transcript complexity is more than a few bits.

assessments.tested_scope: Selector with beta-approximate max-information k bits and fixed-candidate e-process crossing bound.
assessments.rationale: Rogers et al. directly support the max-information bad-event inflation inequality; substituting Ville's fixed-candidate crossing event yields the stated threshold conversion.
limits: Needs a valid full-selector k,beta bound.
Approximate-DP-to-max-information has product-distribution and composition-order caveats.
No matched real-agent experiment.

assessments.tested_scope: Exact validation-independent behavioral equivalence classes only.
assessments.rationale: Aggregating prior mass over exactly test-equivalent behaviors follows the weighted-union construction and aligns with behavior-space PAC-Bayes intuition, but the exact selected-eprocess quotient is a worker synthesis.
limits: Approximate or sample-only equivalence is unsupported.
No empirical power comparison against fresh audit in realistic agents.

assessments.tested_scope: Long-horizon search-agent training with context folding; separated losses, consistency loss and selective-segment training.
assessments.rationale: Primary paper identifies policy-dependent observation shift and reports stable training plus 5.19x training speedup, providing both mechanism-level and quantitative evidence that folding affects the learning-state distribution.
limits: Does not show inference-time folding is harmful in general.
Worker artifact did not inspect full fold-frequency/depth ablations.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: KataGo defenses and adaptive adversaries under the AAAI paper's Go threat model, compute/search settings and defended snapshots.
assessments.rationale: The exact sealed source record and peer-reviewed AAAI primary source show that defenses which stop the known cyclic attack remain vulnerable to freshly optimized attackers; the worker reports 92% and 90% defended-victim win-rate cases with materially lower attacker training compute. This is direct adaptive-evaluation failure evidence.
limits: Narrow Go domain; no quantitative transfer to LLM safety.
Some attack variants weaken at higher victim-search budgets.
Not a full defender-snapshot x independently re-optimized attacker factorial.

assessments.tested_scope: GPT-4.1/Gemini-family agent-control settings with defense-aware prompt optimization on APPS/BashArena and held-out/transfer evaluation.
assessments.rationale: The exact sealed source record reports a 10-iteration proposer-pruner with 31 attempts per defense and primary-table effects including Just Ask Code Backdooring rising from 28% to 68%. The primary paper and released code support the broader conclusion that adaptive optimization can erode static-monitor evaluations while self-incrimination plus monitoring remains stronger in the tested conditions.
limits: Exact percentages remain scoped to the paper's optimization protocol and tasks.
Not prompt-injection evidence and not a universal statement that monitoring fails.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: BEHAVIOR-1K VLA skills evaluated from clean boundary snapshots versus chained terminal states.
assessments.rationale: The exact sealed source record and primary arXiv abstract directly measure a matched handoff distribution shift: selected skills score 77-100% from clean snapshots while chained compositions frequently stall and end-to-end success remains near zero. This strongly supports successor-readiness as a distinct failure mode.
limits: Robotics/VLA scope only.
Diagnoses the failure but does not establish a generic repair mechanism.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Seed-Prover 1.5 formal theorem proving with large-scale agentic RL, Lean/tool interaction and terminal verifier-grounded proof success.
assessments.rationale: The exact sealed C86 record and primary paper independently establish sequential tool-interleaved formal-proof behavior trained by agentic RL with strong Putnam/FATE performance. This closes the broad 'no sequential terminal-reward formal-proof agent' gap at full-model granularity.
limits: Does not isolate a compact typed outer controller.
Binary reward lacks explicit token/$/Lean-time cost objective.
Public 1.5 directory lacks the full trainer/controller trajectory artifact.

assessments.tested_scope: Mistral Leanstral 1.5 formal proof engineering with mid-training/SFT/CISPO RL and open weights/API.
assessments.rationale: The exact sealed C87 record and official July 2, 2026 release report CISPO RL in agentic proof-engineering environments, 587/672 PutnamBench, FATE-H 87%, FATE-X 34%, and Apache-2.0 open weights. Open weights materially strengthen inspectability.
limits: Official release is not an independent replication.
No matched ablation isolates routing/control from general model improvements.
No explicit cost-aware controller objective.

assessments.tested_scope: SkillZip paper and public repository for one-shot/continual compression mechanisms; 16-round LiveMath experiment chronology/replay bundle absent from the inspected public tree.
assessments.rationale: The exact sealed source record plus primary paper support the compression mechanism and continual Zip-on-Write API. The worker's direct public-repository audit supports a narrower reproducibility conclusion: compressor semantics are inspectable, but the original 16-round proposal/accepted-patch chronology and Figure-6 replay bundle were not found.
limits: No independent reconstruction of Figure-6/final-test numbers.
Public tree does not expose accepted-patch chronology or full SkillOpt orchestration in the inspected release.
Structural compression is not behavioral-promotion validity.

assessments.tested_scope: Peer-reviewed astrocyte-gated associative-memory mechanism plus the exact sealed worker's 850 compiled float32 trajectories, literal PyTorch spot checks and matched-seed dt sensitivity for the public Euler implementation.
assessments.rationale: Physical Review Research provides strong primary evidence for the continuous-time mechanism, Lyapunov convergence and retrieval benefit. Separately, the sealed worker numerically localizes negative-p/NaN events to the public dt discontinuity just above tau_p=0.01 and shows smaller scaled dt removes those events for matched seeds while convergence fractions remain unchanged in the tested indices.
limits: The compiled collector is equation-order-equivalent but not bitwise identical to PyTorch; only selected indices received literal PyTorch spot checks.
The numerical defect concerns the public Euler discretization/collector, not the continuous-time mechanism.
No independent external numerical rerun.
